h: The Crown of the Torah: Halachos, Hod and the Taste of Olam HaBa in This World

p: בְּמַאֲמַר תָּנָא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (נִדָּה עג, א)
is with the teaching of Tanna D'vei Eliyahu (Niddah 73a):
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְכוּלֵּי.
"is assured that he is a ben Olam HaBa," etc.
that the meaning of "he is assured"
"that he is a ben Olam HaBa" —
and not the expression "destined for Olam HaBa" —
is that he merits to taste in his lifetime
and while he is still fully alive
he is a ben Olam HaBa,
כְּעִנְיַן עוֹלָמְךָ תִּרְאֶה בְּחַיֶּיךָ (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א)
in the sense of "You shall see your world in your lifetime" (Berachos 17a)
"Three did HaKadosh Baruch Hu give a taste,
בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְכוּלֵּי
in this world, of a semblance of Olam HaBa," etc.:
"Avraham, of whom it is written 'with everything.'"
וְלָזֶה זָכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom, merited this
after he was refined through the tenth test,
as it is written: "And Avraham was old, coming into days"
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קכט, א):
and it says in the holy Zohar (I 129a):
That is, through the tenth test
he was refined in all the middos
הוּא נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to the holiness of Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
who merited the attribute of "old" — Atika;
and after this it is written:
that He gave him a taste of a semblance of Olam HaBa.
And this is what they said: "Whoever learns halachos."
"And one who makes use of the crown," etc. —
"this is one who makes use of one who learns halachos" —
for the halachos come from "the dew of Atika,"
the dew of Torah she'b'al peh,
as it is written: "My speech shall drip like dew"
That is the Torah she'b'al peh
which Hashem Yisbarach causes to shine forth in the hearts of the Sages,
and it cannot be discerned how
it comes down from Heaven, like dew
And this comes through the aspect of Daas,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י (פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא, שְׁמוֹת לא, ג);
as Rashi explained (Parshas Ki Sisa, Shemos 31:3);
הוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב, א)
proving it from the Gemara there:
"Know this, for a great man says something,
and a halachah l'Moshe miSinai is then stated in accordance with him."
And Daas is the inner dimension of Kesser Elyon,
and this is the crown of the Torah.
And so we find with Rabbi Akiva,
who is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
sitting and tying adornments onto the letters," etc.;
"and Akiva ben Yosef is his name,
שֶׁעָתִיד לִדְרוֹשׁ עַל כָּל קוֹץ וָקוֹץ
who is destined to expound upon each and every tip
שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דּוֹרֵשׁ כִּתְרֵי אוֹתִיּוֹת.
for Rabbi Akiva would expound the crowns of the letters.
And about this they said at the conclusion of Shas
which are the crown of the Torah,
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
is assured that he is a ben Olam HaBa —
that he merits to taste in this world
a semblance of Olam HaBa, as stated.

p: וּבְרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רכג, א):
And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Zohar III 223a):
there is no man in the world
who is able to ascend, except Moshe," etc.
That is, Binah — Alma D'asi, the World to Come —
in this world, apart from Moshe.
into the World to Come," etc.
That is, Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
וְאָמַר מַה שֶּׁקַּל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר כֵּן
said something that even the lowest of the low would not say,
for he intended only to establish offspring
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה, בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ע, יח,
(as written in the Midrash Rabbah, Bereishis Rabbah 70:18,
וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י וַיֵּצֵא, בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, כא);
and in Rashi on Vayeitzei, Bereishis 29:21);
of his own pleasure at all,
just like Adam HaRishon before the sin,
of whom it is said "and they were not ashamed"
Rather, he was there from the inner side —
this one from the body and that one from the soul," etc.
וְהָיָה הַפְּנִימִיּוּת מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
He was the inner dimension of Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן
And Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, also
knew nothing of evil at all,
and it says in the Gemara (Sotah 12a):
the entire house was filled with light."
the light "that it was good," which was hidden away.
And it says (in the Ra'aya Meheimna there):
I will ask for the supernal Chochmah,
'I said, I will become wise, but it is far from me'"
This is in the vein of what they said
a Heavenly voice went forth," etc.
וַה׳ נָתַן חָכְמָה לִשְׁלֹמֹה (מְלָכִים א ה, כו).
'And Hashem gave wisdom to Shlomo'" (Melachim I 5:26)!
And it answers: "A small Chochmah, a lower Chochmah."
that one merits to be a ben Olam HaBa,
However (in the Ra'aya Meheimna there, on amud beis),
that the Hod was given to Moshe,
as it says, 'You shall place some of your majesty upon him'"
He said to him: "You have asked well.
The heh rises with the letter yud —
and the fifty gates of Binah," etc.
That is, Chessed, Gevurah and Tiferes —
the Avos are a chariot for them —
and they are the root of Torah she'bi'chsav.
הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁקִּיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ
was the first to fulfill the entire Torah
מִימִינוֹ אֵשׁ דָּת לָמוֹ (דְּבָרִים לג, ב),
"From His right hand, a fiery law for them" (Devarim 33:2),
and "the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג פ, ב);
and of Yaakov it is written,
But they fulfilled the words of Torah
brought the whole Torah down to earth.
is the expansion of Torah she'bi'chsav;
and Hod — Aharon is the chariot for this middah —
and from there Torah she'b'al peh begins.
the Hod was given to Moshe,
and each of the middos is comprised of ten,
are the fifty gates of Binah.
And this is the pilpul that was given to Moshe,
and he dealt generously with it
from there the prophets draw their nourishment;
and it is written: "For the conductor, on the eighth"
"for Netzach does not move away from Hod,
And Aharon HaKohen is the chariot for the middah of Hod;
the bestowing of the Torah she'b'al peh
זֶה נָתַן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְאַהֲרֹן,
this Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, gave to Aharon,
who is the groomsman of the Matrona,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר חֵלֶק ג נג, ב),
for he is the one who purifies and sanctifies Yisrael
so that they can receive in the heart
יוֹרוּ מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְיַעֲקֹב וְגוֹ׳ (דְּבָרִים לג, י),
"They shall teach Your laws to Yaakov," etc. (Devarim 33:10);
and it is written: "For the lips of the Kohen," etc.,
"and they shall seek Torah from his mouth" (Malachi 2:7);
וּכְתִיב וּבָאתָ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים (דְּבָרִים יז, ט),
and it is written: "And you shall come to the Kohanim" (Devarim 17:9),
for they are the teachers of Yisrael.
And Moshe Rabbeinu is the groomsman of the King,
who brought the Torah down to earth.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna) — "Shlomo said: Binah is Moshe's; I will ask for the supernal Chochmah, which is above his level. What is written? 'I said, I will become wise, but it is far from me' (Koheles 7:23). But is it not written, 'And Hashem gave wisdom to Shlomo' (I Melachim 5:26)? A small wisdom… for even to Binah no man in the world can ascend except Moshe — all the more so above it."

paragraphs.text: Taanis 5b — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

p: And so too, the sefirah of Hod begins
וְאִיתָא (בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קנב, ב):
And it says (Ra'aya Meheimna, Zohar III 152b):
"The first Pesach is from the right, where Chochmah is;
the second Pesach is from the left, where Binah is."
That is, the exile of Mitzrayim
was a preparation for Matan Torah;
and on the first Pesach they merited
to be prepared for Matan Torah —
correspond to the five Chumashim of the Torah
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה אָז זְמַן יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם
when it was not then the time of Yetzias Mitzrayim,
so the Pesach to be brought has no connection to it —
about what Moshe said to them:
"Why should we be held back," etc. (ibid. 9:7),
and Moshe told them: stand in prayer,
That is, that they should pray and cry out to Hashem Yisbarach:
And they made the words of Torah
"The second Pesach is from the left, whence Binah" —
that is, understanding one thing out of another,
And this is the matter of placing Naaseh before Nishma:
we will make the words of Torah
and bring down the words of Torah,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה וְנִשְׁמָע.
and afterwards, through this, "we will hear."
"as though he made the words of Torah";
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קי, ב).
and so it is written in the holy Zohar (III 110b).
And through this they merited the crowns,
as it is written: "And wisdom — from Ayin it shall be found"
Atika Stima'ah, the Concealed Ancient One,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר חֵלֶק ב סד, ב).
that they would make the words of Torah,
and afterwards Moshe merited them and took them;
and these are the rays of Hod
that Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, merited.
And this is the meaning of what they said,
that the second Pesach is from the left, where Binah is.
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
It is also the matter of Torah she'b'al peh,
which comes to rectify the "much anger";
for they were indeed impure through a human corpse,
even though it was in a permitted manner
and they were commanded to become impure for a meis mitzvah;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָא נִגְזַר עַל זֶה טוּמְאָה.
nevertheless, impurity was decreed upon this.
And likewise "on a distant road" too
and He provided them a remedy in Pesach Sheni:
"once he has become pure and rectified himself,
there is the second month," etc.
שֶׁמְּתַקְּנִין עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that through the Torah she'b'al peh one rectifies
there the parshah of Pesach Sheni
only from the side of the left,
the hillula of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai,
for then is the sefirah of Hod sheb'Hod;
and to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai were revealed
the reasons of the Torah, the secret of Atika,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קה, ב):
as written in the holy Zohar (III 105b):
after he passed away — 'and for covering the Ancient,'" etc.
And so we find that Rabbi Shimon
expounded the reason of the verse
And even though there these are the revealed aspects
of the reasons of the mitzvos,
with the depth and the secret in the reasons of the mitzvos,
this is one who reveals the things
that the Ancient of Days concealed.
What are they? The reasons of the Torah."
וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי נִתְגַּלָּה זֶה,
And to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai this was revealed,
in the sefirah of Hod sheb'Hod.
וְאִיתָא בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רכג, א):
And it says in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Zohar III 223a):
when he reached the three upper sefiros,
ה׳ לֹא גָבַהּ לִבִּי וְלֹא רָמוּ עֵינַי
'Hashem, my heart was not haughty, nor were my eyes raised,
nor did I pursue matters too great and too wondrous for me'"
That is: "my heart was not haughty"
corresponds to the middah of Chochmah — the brain.
And the Sanhedrin are called "the eyes of the congregation,"
"May your eyes shine with the light of Torah."
And the eyes correspond to the brain,
as it says: "between your eyes," etc.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג פא, א):
as written in the holy Zohar (III 81a):
in the utterance "Let there be light,"
correspond to the five Chumashim of the Torah,
And about this: "nor were my eyes raised,"
and "nor did I pursue matters too great and too wondrous for me"
which is the intellect hidden from all thought,
And so the term "great things" indicates,
regarding Hashem Yisbarach, something without measure;
for if it were with measure,
there would be something greater than it,
רַק גָּדוֹל — מַה שֶּׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִתְּפִיסָה,
Rather, "great" is that which is beyond grasp,
the intellect hidden from all thought.
וְהוּא כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יא, ב):
This is akin to what they said (Chagigah 11b):
"One might think a person may ask
about what preceded the creation of the world;
אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא ה׳ אָדָם עַל הָאָרֶץ
that Hashem created man upon the earth'"
That is, the seven lower middos
are the seven days of Creation —
which Hashem Yisbarach emanated for the creation of the world;
"One might think a person may not ask
about the six days of Creation;
the verse teaches: 'Of the earliest days
for which the seven shepherds are a chariot,
and in all Yisrael there is an extension of their holiness,
since they are the Avos and the shepherds —
that is, to ascend into the World to Come,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רז, א)
But the Avos are a chariot
for the three middos of Chessed, Gevurah and Tiferes.
Netzach and Hod — from there the prophets draw their nourishment;
and from Hod is the expansion
of the fifty gates of Binah,
And afterwards it says (in the Ra'aya Meheimna there):
and took all fifty gates," etc.,
וְאוּף הָכִי כַּלָּה נְטִילַת לְהוּ כּוּלְּהוּ וְכוּלֵּי.
"and likewise the Kallah took them all," etc.
For the middah of Malchus is called Kallah,
for Kol, whose letters equal fifty, corresponds to the fifty gates of Binah;
and the heh is the middah of Malchus —
פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרִינַן לָהּ.
"Peh — Torah she'b'al peh we call it."
And "a sage is greater than a prophet";
meaning "a spirit from that supernal Kodesh"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סא, א);
which is the inner dimension of Kesser Elyon.
רַק זֶה זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי הַהַמְשָׁכָה
But this is merited through the drawing down
from the fifty gates of Binah
שֶׁהוּא מַלְכוּת, פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
which is Malchus, Peh, Torah she'b'al peh.
And this is the concept of the "lens that does not shine"
from where the prophets draw their nourishment,
and they correspond to Moshe and Aharon.
one is greater than a prophet,
and they merit the fiftieth gate,
רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְכוּלֵּי
the eye of Rabbi Akiva saw," etc.
And this is what they said at the conclusion of the Talmud:
for they are the crown of the Torah.
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנח, א).
And the crown-tip of the yud
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם סה, ב):
as written in the holy Zohar (ibid. 65b):
"The upper tip of the yud alludes to Ayin" —
which is what is written: "And wisdom — from Ayin it shall be found";
the most concealed of all, which is called Ayin
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב סד, ב).
That is, it shines forth from the crown of the Torah,
the dew of the Torah she'b'al peh;
וְזֶה מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and this is "he is assured that he is a ben Olam HaBa" —
that he merits to taste in this world
a semblance of Olam HaBa, as stated.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, Beshalach 64b — “Rabbi Abba said: What is meant by ‘Is the Lord in our midst, or nothing?’ Were Israel fools who did not know this matter? Had they not seen the Divine Presence before them and the clouds of glory surrounding them? ... Rather, Rabbi Shimon said this: They wished to know the difference between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, who is called Nothing, and Zeir Anpin, who is called the Lord. ... Why, then, were they punished? Because they made a separation and put it to a test. They said: If it is this One, we will ask in one manner; if it is this One, we will ask in another manner. Therefore, immediately, ‘Amalek came.’” The Zohar interprets Israel's question at Massah as a question about the degree from which Divine governance was being revealed. It explicitly names the concealed Atika as Ayin.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88a — “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' six hundred thousand ministering angels came, and tied two crowns to each individual of Israel, one corresponding to 'We will do' and one to 'We will hear.' When Israel sinned, twelve hundred thousand destructive angels descended and removed them, as it says: 'The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Chorev.' Rabbi Yochanan said: Moshe merited them all and took them. Reish Lakish said: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will return them to us, as it says: 'Those redeemed by Hashem will return and come to Zion with song, with everlasting joy upon their heads'—the joy that had been upon their heads from of old. Rabbi Elazar said: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' a heavenly voice went forth: 'Who revealed to My children this secret used by the ministering angels?' For it is written: 'Bless Hashem, His angels, mighty in strength, who perform His word, to hear the voice of His word'—first performing, and afterward hearing.” This is the source both for the two crowns and for the angelic precedence of doing over hearing. Its account of Moshe receiving the lost crowns and their eventual restoration also underlies the ensuing discussion.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a — “May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be life in the World to Come, your hope for every generation. May your heart meditate understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your tongue utter songs. ... May your eyes shine with the light of Torah and your face radiate like the brightness of the firmament; may your lips express knowledge, your innermost parts rejoice in uprightness, and your steps run to hear the words of the Ancient of Days.” This blessing distinguishes seeing one's world during life from one's final life in the World to Come. Its conjunction of understanding, speech, song, and the Ancient of Days particularly illuminates Rav Tzadok's present interpretation.

p: And as for what they said,
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
"he is assured that he is a ben Olam HaBa,"
meaning he is assured that he will not go astray —
אַל תַּאֲמִין בְּעַצְמְךָ עַד יוֹם מוֹתְךָ,
"Do not trust yourself until the day of your death,
served in the High Priesthood for eighty years
and in the end became a Tzeduki."
that there is only one world
and denied the Resurrection of the Dead
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן פֶּרֶק ה),
(as written in Avos D'Rabbi Nosson, chapter 5);
וְאָמְרוּ אֵין עוֹלָם אֶלָּא אֶחָד וְכוּלֵּי;
and said there is only one world," etc.;
and one who denies the Resurrection of the Dead
has no portion in Olam HaBa
who was worthy that the Shechinah rest upon him,
and when he died they said of him:
that the Torah be given to Yisrael through him,
had Moshe not preceded him," etc.
had he not already begun it,
שֶׁמָּא נִתְקַלְקֵל וְנַעֲשָׂה מִין חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
of perhaps having gone astray and become a heretic, chas v'shalom
So how does it say here,
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא?
"he is assured that he is a ben Olam HaBa"?
But in truth, what we learned
שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי לֹא יוּכַל לִסְמוֹךְ עַל עַצְמוֹ,
that certainly he cannot rely on himself,
even if he has attained the whole Torah,
that he will surely not go astray;
שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכָל יוֹם,
for the yetzer hara overpowers him every day,
and "whoever is greater than his fellow,
his yetzer is greater than he"
and it could, chas v'shalom, lead him astray.
אַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
But nonetheless, through the words of Torah,
ה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ (תְּהִלִּים לז, לג).
"Hashem will not abandon him into his hand" (Tehillim 37:33).
who was the root of Torah she'b'al peh
and would expound the crowns of the letters,
that the Satan said to him:
"Were it not that they proclaim about you in Heaven,
'Beware of Rabbi Akiva and his Torah,'" etc.;
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ שָׁם גַּבֵּי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
and so we find there regarding Rabbi Meir.
That is, had they, chas v'shalom,
לֹא הָיָה בְּכֹחָם לִכְבּוֹשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע;
they would not have had the strength to conquer the yetzer hara;
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם
only through their words of Torah —
"Hashem will not abandon him into his hand" —
and they proclaimed about them in Heaven:
"Beware of Rabbi Akiva and his Torah,"
"Beware of Rabbi Meir and his Torah."
וְאָמַר שֶׁלֹּא רַק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
And it says that not only Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Meir and their like,
which is the crown of the Torah,
זוֹכֶה אֲשֶׁר ה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ
merits that "Hashem will not abandon him into his hand,"
וּמוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
and is assured that he is a ben Olam HaBa.
that of himself he has no strength to prevail,
only with the help of Hashem Yisbarach, as stated.
And so it is expounded (Bava Basra 17a),
that the yetzer hara had no dominion over them
and the Angel of Death had no dominion over them.
So too, anyone who learns halachos,
זוֹכֶה שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע —
merits that the yetzer hara will not dominate him —
"Hashem will not abandon him into his hand" —
and that the Angel of Death will not dominate him.
Even though the entire blemish has not been rectified,
וְלֹא זָכוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי מַמָּשׁ
and they have not merited to be truly in the World to Come
that death will be for him merely like sleep,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָקִיצוּ וְרַנְּנוּ (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יט)
"'When you lie down, it shall guard over you' — this is death;
'and when you awaken, it shall converse with you' — in the time to come,"
so that it will be merely like waking from sleep
וְיוּכַל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה
And every one of Yisrael can merit this
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁשּׁוֹנֶה הֲלָכוֹת בְּכָל יוֹם:

paragraphs.text: Commentary: Ben Ish Chai, Ben Yehoyada on Bava Basra 17a — “‘Three the Holy One, blessed be He, gave a taste in this world of the World to Come’: this does not mean they lacked no good, for many troubles passed over them; rather… He gave the Avos in this world a great joy in Torah and mitzvos, which is the joy of the World to Come… ‘Three, the yetzer hara had no dominion over them’: it seems to me that in every tzaddik the yetzer hara can raise a little evil desire, and he pushes it away.” Connection: The Ben Yehoyada explains the Avos' taste of the World to Come and their freedom from the yetzer hara, the two things the maamar weighs.
